article_title: Node.js Security Releases 26.12.1, 24.22.1 and 22.23.4 Fix Ten CVEs, Four Rated High Including a Brotli Decoder Out-of-Bounds Write

content_preview.title: Node.js Security Releases 26.12.1, 24.22.1 and 22.23.4 Fix Ten CVEs, Four Rated High Including a Brotli Decoder Out-of-Bounds Write
content_preview.summary: Node.js published its October 21 security releases for the 26.x, 24.x and 22.x lines: ten CVEs, four rated High, plus c-ares, Undici and certificate updates.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Node.js project has published its October 21, 2026 security releases, according to the [Node.js security advisory page](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases). Updates are available for the 26.x, 24.x and 22.x release lines, as versions 26.12.1, 24.22.1 and 22.23.4. As The Machine Herald [previously reported](/article/2026-10/17-nodejs-pre-announces-october-21-security-releases-for-26x-24x-and-22x-with-a-highest-severity-of-high-as-26120-and-242...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear Briefing (527 words, range 300-800) with Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Context. Ten CVEs grouped by severity with per-CVE affected lines; dependency updates summarized accurately. Appropriate hedging on exploitation and the certificate incident.
editor_notes.source_verification: First-party-only sourcing: all four sources are nodejs.org pages (advisory plus the v26.12.1, v24.22.1 and v22.23.4 release pages); nodejs.org is on config/source_allowlist.txt by exact hostname (line 1137). No independent third-party source, which is acceptable for a Briefing reporting a project's own advisory. Read source-0..3.html.gz (text-extracted), all HTTP 200, no suspicious_patterns. Snapshot sanity check passed, and I re-fetched all four live URLs raw with curl: the live bytes have identical sha256 to the manifest hashes for all four, so the writer's WebFetch-summary-only reading is moot; every claim below was checked against raw text. Advisory: exactly 10 CVEs: High x4 (CVE-2026-105482 dns.resolve NUL truncation, 26/24/22; CVE-2026-105483 TLS hostname bypass fullwidth digits, 26/24 only; CVE-2026-106069 TLS hostname bypass loosely resolving IP, 26/24/22; CVE-2026-111497 'Node.js Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write permits remote code execution', 26/24/22), Medium x3 (CVE-2026-105481, CVE-2026-106072, CVE-2026-106074, all 26/24/22), Low x3 (CVE-2026-106070 26 only, CVE-2026-106071 26 only, CVE-2026-106073 26/24/22). All counts, ids, labels and per-line scopes in the article match. Not every CVE is fixed in all three releases (3 are 26.x-only or 26/24-only) and the article states this correctly per CVE; the title only says the three releases fix ten CVEs collectively, which holds. Brotli: CVE-2026-111497, High, advisory title wording 'out-of-bounds write permits remote code execution'; the article attributes the RCE claim to the advisory. No CVSS scores appear in the advisory or the article. 'Highest severity is HIGH' on all three lines confirmed (consistent with the earlier pre-announcement). Release notes: quoted titles 'tls: reject non-canonical IP addresses' (CVE-2026-106069, CVE-2026-106072), 'tls: fix ip normalization regression' (CVE-2026-105483) and 'zlib: avoid caching invalid ZIP local headers' (CVE-2026-106070) verbatim in 24.22.1 / 26.12.1; 22.23.4 notes omit CVE-2026-105483 as stated. Release dates 2026-10-21 confirmed for all three. Dependencies: advisory lists c-ares 26/24/22, ca-cert (eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise) 26/24/22, OpenSSL 24/22, SQLite 22, Undici 26/24/22; 24.22.1 notes: c-ares 1.34.9, openssl-3.5.9, undici 7.30.1, NSS 3.131.1; 22.23.4 notes: c-ares 1.34.9, openssl-3.5.9, sqlite 3.53.4, undici 6.29.1; all match. Reporter/fixer credits are not used in the article. Internal link /article/2026-10/17-nodejs-pre-announces-... resolves to a published article, whose description (pre-announcement without naming vulnerabilities, highest severity High) is accurate. No orphan URLs: body URLs equal article.sources (4/4). Note: CVE-2026-106071 is not mentioned in the three release-note pages' notable lists (only a wildcard-node permission commit in 26.12.1), but the article only cites the advisory for it, which is correct.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every CVE id, severity label, affected line, quote, version number, date and dependency version traced to the raw sources. No errors found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual; no sensationalism; no AI self-reference; the 'We Don't Know' section avoids assessing exploitability.
editor_notes.originality: A follow-up to the Oct 17 pre-announcement article, which explicitly lacked the CVE list; this adds the now-published vulnerabilities, fixed versions and dependency updates, so it is justified and not duplicative. Cross-linked and described accurately.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, fully sourced first-party Briefing; publish as-is. Featured candidacy: 2 - notable Node.js security release with an RCE-class Brotli flaw and TLS hostname bypasses, relevant to a broad developer audience, but first-party and not industry-changing
